# Results — Study 227 (Natgas-Winter): is the winter natural-gas spike a tradable season?

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Monthly returns of **UNG (United States
Natural Gas Fund)** built from daily closes resampled to month-end on a verified hole-free grid:
2007-05 → 2026-05, **229 months, zero interior holes** — every calendar month from UNG inception.
As-of 2026-06-01; inputs fingerprint `68346ee6801f`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `NONE` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Winter is a tailwind"? `BUSTED`

The famous winter-demand thesis **does not survive roll drag**. A seasonal long that buys UNG each
October and holds through March earns **−3.56%/month on average in those months** versus **−0.04%/month
in summer** — winter is the *worst* season, not the best. The regression slope on the winter dummy is
**−0.035 (t = −1.96)**: not only the wrong sign for a seasonal edge, but barely shy of the 2.0 bar
(and entirely driven by contango drag). The seasonal strategy CAGR is **−24.5%/yr** versus buy-and-hold
UNG at **−28.2%/yr** — both catastrophic, and the one-sided Sharpe comparison (−0.60 vs −0.45) merely
reflects that concentrating losses in winter is even worse than holding through summer too. `BUSTED`.

- **Ticker**: UNG (United States Natural Gas Fund LP), 2007-05-31 → 2026-05-31, **229 months,

- **Construction**: daily closes resampled to month-end (last close of each calendar month). The

## No winter edge — the slope is the wrong sign

| Winter-dummy regression (Oct-Mar = 1, Apr-Sep = 0) | value |
|---|---|
| slope (winter premium) | **−0.035** (positive slope would support the claim) |
| t-stat | **−1.96** (need |t| ≥ 2; even this is the wrong sign) |
| mean monthly return, Oct-Mar | **−3.56%** |
| mean monthly return, Apr-Sep | **−0.04%** |
| n | 229 |

Winter is the *worst* season for UNG. A positive slope would mean winter months outperform — instead
the estimate is negative in both sub-periods (−0.99 and −1.72) and the full period. The roll-drag
toll peaks in winter as the market prices the heating-season premium into the curve; by the time you
buy UNG in October, that premium is already baked into the front-month price and you pay it away as
you roll into cheaper (or more distant) contracts.

## …and the seasonal strategy is worse than simply holding

| | CAGR | Sharpe | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|
| seasonal (long Oct-Mar, cash = 0 Apr-Sep) | **−24.5%** | **−0.60** | −100% |
| buy & hold UNG | **−28.2%** | **−0.45** | −100% |

Both strategies destroy capital at an alarming rate. Concentrating exposure in the winter months —
when roll drag is highest and the curve is most steeply contangoed — is even more destructive than
buying and holding year-round. The seasonal Sharpe (−0.60) is *worse* than buy-and-hold (−0.45).

## It is never significant in either sub-period

| | slope | t | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2007–2015 | −0.020 | −0.99 | 104 |
| 2016–2026 | −0.048 | −1.72 | 125 |

Neither sub-period shows a positive, significant winter premium. The 2016–2026 period actually has a
larger negative slope (−0.048 vs −0.020), suggesting roll drag has intensified rather than decayed.

## The widow-maker explained

UNG holds front-month natural-gas futures and rolls them before expiry into the next contract.
When the futures curve is in contango (the standard condition in natural gas: nearby contracts are
cheaper than later ones because storage holders must be compensated), each monthly roll sells the
cheap nearby and buys the expensive next contract — a guaranteed monthly loss even if spot prices
don't move. This "roll yield drag" can run −2% to −5%/month in winter when the curve is most
steeply sloped. Over a 5-month winter season (Oct-Mar), the cumulative drag can exceed −15% before
a single cent of spot-price appreciation.

## The honest takeaway

"Winter natural-gas demand creates a tradable UNG seasonal" is a `MIRAGE` on the full live history
of UNG: winter is the *worst* season (−3.56%/month), the premium regression slope is negative
(t = −1.96), and the seasonal strategy Sharpe (−0.60) is worse than buy-and-hold (−0.45). The
widow-maker earns its name. `NONE`, `MIRAGE`, `BUSTED`.
